notes: The brief is met. The interval is checked server-side when the cookie is written (set_refresh, packet-judge.md:194) and again when home() reads it (packet-judge.md:115). A hand-edited cookie like "1" falls back to off, and the noscript meta-refresh and data-refresh appear only on the home page. The JS countdown holds and says so while a field is focused or non-empty, and it correctly skips the always-filled hidden inputs, a real bug the self-review found and fixed (packet-judge.md:89). The 30 s badge cache lives in pipeline.gpu_node_online_cached (packet-judge.md:231), and transcribe() still probes live; a test proves it (packet-judge.md:39 of the test tail, test_transcribe_routes_on_a_live_probe_not_the_badge_cache). The one real defect: 'Refresh now' is <button onclick="location.reload()"> (packet-judge.md:148), so it does nothing in the JS-less browser the brief explicitly serves. The reference uses <a href="/">. That one-line fix is the MINOR. The 7 hidden reference-test failures are almost all interface-naming coupling, not behaviour bugs: REFRESH_CHOICES and _gpu_status do not exist, the form field is 'interval' not 'seconds', the countdown span is empty instead of 'refreshing in Ns', and the 'location.reload' string from that onclick is on the page even when auto-refresh is off. The candidate's tests call handlers directly with fakes rather than going through an HTTP client with a real cookie round trip, and the hold logic is not exercised. trading_risk n/a: this is not a trading system.
